title: Metadichol as a Coordinated Activator of Core Cellular Machinery. Part III—Metadichol Induces Selective Remodeling of Nuclear Pore Complex Gene Expression in Human Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells: A Comprehensive Quantitative RT-PCR Analysis
content: Background: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) serves as the sole gateway for macromolecular exchange between the nucleus and cytoplasm, and its ~30 constituent nucleoporin (NUP) proteins are critical regulators of gene expression, immune function, and cellular identity. Metadichol, a nano-emulsion of long-chain polycosanols, exhibits pleiotropic biological activities including immunomodulatory and transcription-regulatory effects; however, its influence on NPC gene expression has not previously been characterized. Objectives: To evaluate dose-dependent effects of metadichol on expression of 31 NPC-associated genes in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) using quantitative RT-PCR. Methods: PBMCs were treated with metadichol at concentrations from 0.1 pg/mL to 100 ng/mL. Total RNA was extracted, reverse-transcribed, and analyzed by SYBR Green qRT-PCR using the 2⁻ΔΔCq method with GAPDH normalization.Results: Metadichol induced selective, concentration-dependent NPC gene modulation. Consistent upregulation was observed in GLE1 (up to 1.52-fold), NUP358 (1.94-fold), NUP210 (2.03-fold), and NDC1 (2.18-fold). Significant downregulation was documented in NUP54 (minimum 0.26-fold), ELYS, NUP214, and multiple Y-complex scaffold components. Biphasic responses were identified for NUP205, TPR, NUP35, and NUP107. Conclusions: Metadichol orchestrates functional NPC reorganization—suppressing structural scaffold elements while selectively enhancing nucleocytoplasmic transport. Network analysis implicates converging regulatory inputs from circadian, SIRT, FOX, KLF, and TLR gene families. These findings open new avenues for investigating metadichol in immune regulation and cellular reprogramming.
